name: Lustre firing
summary: A thin film of copper or silver on a glazed pot gives a metallic shine. The potter paints a pigment on the glaze and fires it in smoke at a low heat.
how: Mix a copper or silver compound with clay and vinegar to make a paste.
Paint the paste on the fired glaze.
Fire the pot at 600 to 800 °C and fill the kiln with smoke in the second half.
Wash off the clay after the firing to show the metallic film.

origin.note: Potters of Basra paint metal pigments on tin-glazed pots and fire them in smoke to make a gold sheen.

adoptions.via: William De Morgan tests lustre in Chelsea and makes ruby and gold lustre tiles and vases in London.
